why_relevant: NABU hosts per-member profile pages (banks and partner associations alike — the example is its profile of the Ukrainian Association of Fintech and Innovation Companies). The directory is effectively a curated map of every banking-sector actor worth scouting, and each profile links out to the member's own site, which is where its own leadership pages live.

Governance page of the Ukrainian Interbank Association of Payment System Members (EMA/ЄМА). Search evidence indicates the General Assembly of 24 October 2025 formed a new Board comprising Mastercard, Visa and the major Ukrainian banks (PrivatBank, Raiffeisen, Oschadbank, Sens Bank, UkrSibbank, PUMB, Universal Bank, Ukrgasbank, OTP Bank, VST Bank), with a named Board Chair. This is the single highest-precision payments-side roster of who currently represents each issuer/acquirer.

source_name: EMA Association — About / newsroom (AntiFraud HUB, EMA Academy)
why_relevant: EMA runs operational working groups and programmes (AntiFraud HUB, EMA Academy, API Group) whose coordinators and speaker rosters are drawn from serving bank security/payments heads. Announcements of working-group leads and speakers are a secondary, higher-frequency read on who occupies operational senior roles between formal Board elections.

source_name: AUB (Association of Ukrainian Banks) — Rada AUB (Council)
why_relevant: AUB is the older of the two banking associations (70+ member banks and non-bank financial companies). Its Council has 13 seats — President and First Vice-President ex officio plus 11 elected bank representatives — so the roster is a direct list of serving senior bankers. The presidency itself is a tracked leadership post (Andrii Bohdanovych reported as president as of Dec 2025; historically Oleksandr Suhoniako).

AUB's sectoral committees are chaired by serving bank executives; the committee list plus chairs is a second, finer-grained slice of the same senior-position map, and committee reshuffles often precede or follow bank-level appointments.

70+ member organisations including state and commercial banks plus non-bank financial companies — the complementary actor map to EMA's (banking-weighted rather than payments-weighted), and the union of the two is close to a full census of the addressable market.

AUB's news archive reports congress outcomes, council elections and cross-association bodies. The linked example documents the creation of a Coordination Council of professional financial-market participants jointly by AUB, PFTS, the Stock Market Lawyers Association, the League of Insurance Organisations and others — i.e. it snowballs into a whole further layer of sectoral bodies whose leaderships are worth mapping.

source_name: American Chamber of Commerce in Ukraine — Banking & Financial Services Committee
why_relevant: A self-organising sectoral committee whose co-chairs and 'Responsible Board Member' are serving executives — evidence names Steven Fisher (CEO/Chairman of the Board, Citibank Ukraine) as responsible board member, Taras Kyrychenko (Pravex-Bank) and Ihor Olekhov (Baker McKenzie) among members, and a separate release records Olekhov's election as committee co-chair. Committee co-chair elections are announced and dated, giving an English-language, high-precision leadership feed for the international-bank segment.

source_name: U.S.-Ukraine Business Council (USUBC) member-news — committee election announcements
why_relevant: Republishes member firms' announcements of association/committee appointments in English, often persisting after the originating page rotates. Useful as an archival mirror and for cross-checking dates on committee-chair elections.

source_name: European Business Association (EBA Ukraine) — committees and committee-chair elections
why_relevant: EBA runs sectoral committees whose chairs are elected from serving executives and whose elections are published as dated releases (verified pattern: the Ukraine Recovery Committee chair election of 19 Dec 2025). EBA's financial-sector committees carry the same pattern, and EBA leadership itself (long chaired in the past by ex-banker Roman Shpek) sits at the banking/policy interface.

Third banking association, uniting a reported 92 financial and credit institutions across all regions plus foreign institutions (founded 1994 as the Kyiv Banking Union, renamed 2005). Adds member banks and regional institutions that NABU/AUB rosters may miss, and its own council/presidency is a leadership post.

source_name: All-Ukrainian Association of Financial Companies (VAFK / ВАФК)
why_relevant: Represents non-bank financial companies (registered 2016, EDRPOU 40337251; head recorded in the registry as Saviuk Alla Volodymyrivna). Non-bank finance companies are a significant slice of Ukraine's payments/lending market and a hiring source for bank and fintech executives; the association publishes rules, positions and member material.

source_name: All-Ukrainian Association of Credit Unions (VAKS) — Council page
why_relevant: One of the two national credit-union associations (registered 2004, EDRPOU 33349572; director recorded as Tuhai Olha Oleksandrivna). It maintains a dedicated 'Рада ВАКС' page listing council members drawn from serving credit-union heads — the cooperative-finance edge of the same who-holds-what map, and relevant to payments as credit unions adopt card/payment services.

source_name: National Association of Credit Unions of Ukraine (NAKSU)
why_relevant: The second national credit-union association (also indexed at unascu.org.ua), distinct from VAKS. Completes the cooperative-finance actor map and provides an English-language section, useful for cross-language name resolution of the same executives.

Professional platform joining practitioners from business, financial institutions, the legal community and state bodies. Compliance/AML heads are a senior banking function tracked in A5; the association's board, speakers and certification cohorts name the people currently holding those roles.

source_name: Opendatabot / YouControl / Clarity Project registry cards for the associations themselves
why_relevant: Every association is itself a registered legal entity whose signatory/head changes are recorded in the state register and surfaced by these aggregators — EMA (EDRPOU 30401000), UAFIC (42031209), VAFK (40337251), VAKS (33349572), UKBS (21573585). This gives a dated, authoritative corroboration channel for association-leadership changes that is independent of whether the association updates its own website, and covers cases where the website is stale or JS-blocked.

source_name: Ukrainian Wikipedia articles on the banking associations
why_relevant: Maintains historical succession lists (past chairs/presidents, renaming history, membership counts) for NABU and AUB. Valuable for entity resolution and for building a time series of who held association posts before the current snapshot, which the associations' own sites rarely retain.

source_name: International Financial Club BANKIR — speaker rosters for banking forums
why_relevant: Association-adjacent industry club whose forum speaker pages (e.g. Banking Forum: Digital Trends 2026) publish name + current title + institution for dozens of serving executives at a time, in both uk and en. High-yield, dated snapshots of who currently occupies senior banking/payments roles, complementary to formal association rosters.
